_meta.purpose: Question set for the 'test honesty' dimension: does a test, as written in its file, check what its title states? Everything under `request_template` follows the documented request schema of POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (top-level `state`, `model`, `questions`; each question has `type`, `instructions`, `criteria`). `_meta` is for the harness and is never sent.
_meta.provenance: Drafted only from SPEC.md, labels.dev.json, the referenced test files in HardwareVisualizer, and https://docs.typesafe.ai. No other source was consulted.
_meta.model_note: Pinned version id, not the `jev-latest` alias. The docs say an alias moves on release and that thresholds tuned on one version should pin that version. Log the `model` field of every response.
_meta.question_id_note: Ids are never sent to the model (documented). They exist so code can group the answers of one test. Every question therefore names its target inside `instructions`.

placeholders.{file_path}: Repository-relative path of the test file.
placeholders.{numbered_source}: The entire test file, verbatim, each line prefixed with its line id and a pipe: `L0066| it("...", () => {`. Line id = 'L' + 1-based line number zero-padded to 4 digits.
placeholders.{test_key}: Key of one target test inside `state.target_tests`: 't' + zero-padded start line, e.g. `t0066`. Unique within a file even when titles repeat.
placeholders.{title}: The test's title exactly as written in the file (the raw template for it.each titles, e.g. '... is %s').
placeholders.{describe_path}: Titles of the enclosing describe blocks, outermost first, joined with ' > '. Empty string when the test is at top level.
placeholders.{start_line}: 1-based line number of the line that opens the test call (it/test/it.each). This is the `line` field of labels.dev.json.
placeholders.{end_line}: 1-based line number of the line that closes the test call.
placeholders.{start_line_id}: {start_line} rendered as a line id, e.g. `L0066`.
placeholders.{end_line_id}: {end_line} rendered as a line id, e.g. `L0079`.
placeholders.{test_code}: Lines {start_line}..{end_line} copied from {numbered_source}, line ids included.
placeholders.{own_snippet}: Control only. A short literal (call expression or string literal, one line) that occurs inside the target test and nowhere else in the file. Chosen by code.
placeholders.{sibling_snippet}: Control only. A short literal that occurs inside the nearest other test of the same file and not inside the target test. Chosen by code.

polarity_legend.problem: Higher answer = more evidence that the test does not check what its title states.
polarity_legend.undecidable: Higher answer = more evidence that this file alone cannot settle the matter. Not evidence of a problem and not evidence of health.
polarity_legend.control: The correct answer is known to the harness from static parsing. Used only to detect that the judge is looking at the wrong test. Never part of the suspicion value.

assertion_specificity.read: probabilities of the top levels; level order runs from fine (0) to worst (last)

verdict.polarity: mixed: `does_not_verify` and `verifies_part` are problem, `cannot_tell_from_file` is undecidable, `verifies` is health
verdict.read: choice, probabilities, confidence. Used for the cannot-tell rule and as a cross-check; not part of the suspicion value in v1.

state_variants.primary: Object state as in `request_template.state`: the whole numbered file under `source`, plus one entry per asked-about test under `target_tests`. The test's code is duplicated there on purpose so that questions can address it with a backticked path (the documented way to point a question at part of the state) instead of asking the model to find a line range by number.
state_variants.control: State is `{ "file_path": ..., "source": ... }` only (no `target_tests`). In every question replace `target_tests.{test_key}.code` with `the test described in target_test` and `target_tests.{test_key}.title` with `target_test.title`. Run the dev set under both variants; keep the one with fewer control failures and fewer missing-context false flags.

_meta.budget_note: Documented limits for jev-1.13.0: 64k tokens per request for state plus all questions; 32k tokens for state plus the single longest question. One test costs 12 questions. Chunk the tests of one file over several requests when needed; a file whose numbered source alone approaches the 32k limit cannot be judged in this version and must be reported as not judged.

instructions.question: Do the assertions in `target_tests.{test_key}.code` all check something other than the outcome stated in `target_tests.{test_key}.title`?
instructions.setup_scope: Setup counts wherever it appears in `source`: module-level mocks and the default values they return, hoisted mock objects, beforeEach and beforeAll hooks of every enclosing describe block, helper and fixture functions the test calls, and mocked translation tables that turn keys into the texts the assertions look for.

criteria.true: The title states an outcome, and no expect in the test would fail if that outcome stopped happening. The expects check other things, such as a message, a log call, an unrelated field, or only that something exists.
criteria.false: At least one expect checks the stated outcome itself, either directly or at a mocked boundary that the title is about. An expect inside a helper function that the test calls counts.

instructions.question: Does `target_tests.{test_key}.title` describe what a result contains, while the assertions in `target_tests.{test_key}.code` only check that a function was called?

criteria.true: The title describes a resulting value, order, list or state. Every expect only checks that a mock or spy was called, or how many times, without checking its arguments or anything it produced.
criteria.false: An expect checks call arguments, a return value, rendered output or stored state. Or the title only says that an action is triggered, and the call itself is that action.

instructions.question: Does `target_tests.{test_key}.title` say that a particular function is called or is not called, while no assertion in `target_tests.{test_key}.code` inspects the calls of that function?

criteria.true: The title is about a call happening or not happening, and the expects only look at values, state or rendered output.
criteria.false: An expect inspects the calls of the function the title names: called, not called, or called with. Or the title is not about a function call.

instructions.question: Does `target_tests.{test_key}.code` run without ever creating, passing or comparing the condition, input or mechanism that `target_tests.{test_key}.title` names?
instructions.setup_scope: Setup counts wherever it appears in `source`: module-level mocks and the default values they return, hoisted mock objects, beforeEach and beforeAll hooks of every enclosing describe block, helper and fixture functions the test calls, and mocked translation tables that turn keys into the texts the assertions look for.

criteria.true: Even counting shared setup, nothing in the test creates, passes or compares the thing the title names. Examples: the title names an ordering clause and nothing in the test involves order; the title names a locale and no locale is set or compared; the title is about one item among others being skipped and the input holds no items at all.
criteria.false: The named condition is created in the test body or in shared setup, even if no line of the test body mentions it. Or it is simply the initial state before anything has happened.

instructions.question: Does `target_tests.{test_key}.title` state a second behaviour or detail that no assertion in `target_tests.{test_key}.code` checks?

criteria.true: The title joins two or more checkable claims, for example with 'and', 'with', 'only', 'per' or 'so'. At least one of them is asserted, and at least one other has no expect that would fail if it broke.
criteria.false: Every checkable claim in the title has an expect, or the title states a single claim. Wording that only explains why the behaviour matters, or how it is meant to be used, is not a claim.

instructions.question: Does `target_tests.{test_key}.title` generalise over every, each, all, only or repeated occurrences, while `target_tests.{test_key}.code` exercises a single occurrence?

criteria.true: The title generalises, with words such as every update, each item, only when, again or always. The test triggers the behaviour once or with one item, so the general claim and a narrower one would pass alike.
criteria.false: The test exercises several occurrences or contrasting cases. Or other tests in the same describe block of `source` exercise the contrasting cases. Or the title does not generalise.

instructions.question: Is `target_tests.{test_key}.title` too vague to name an expected result?

criteria.true: The title only says that the code works, handles something, or behaves correctly or properly, without saying what the result should be.
criteria.false: The title names a concrete behaviour or result.

instructions.question: How specific are the assertions in `target_tests.{test_key}.code`?
instructions.focus: Judge the strongest expect in the test. An expect inside a helper function that the test calls counts.

criteria: At least one expect compares a produced value, rendered text, stored state or call arguments against an exact expected value, or asserts that a specific thing is absent.
The strongest expect only matches a pattern or a partial shape: a regular expression, a substring, 'some element matches', or a loose inequality.
The expects only check that something exists, is defined, is non-empty, has a type or has some length, or that a function was called without checking its arguments.

instructions.question: Is `target_tests.{test_key}.code` arranged around a particular number, limit or timing rule that is not stated anywhere in `source`?

criteria.true: The test repeats an event a particular number of times, waits a particular time, or picks a particular size, and whether that is enough to trigger the behaviour in the title depends on a limit defined in the code under test that is neither shown nor mentioned in this file.
criteria.false: The inputs and expected values speak for themselves, or the relevant number is defined or mentioned in this file, including in a comment. Merely calling imported code does not count.

instructions.question: Judging only from `source`, how do the assertions in `target_tests.{test_key}.code` relate to what `target_tests.{test_key}.title` states?
instructions.setup_scope: Setup counts wherever it appears in `source`: module-level mocks and the default values they return, hoisted mock objects, beforeEach and beforeAll hooks of every enclosing describe block, helper and fixture functions the test calls, and mocked translation tables that turn keys into the texts the assertions look for.

criteria.verifies: At least one expect would fail if the behaviour stated in the title broke.
criteria.verifies_part: The main behaviour in the title is asserted, and another behaviour or detail stated in the title is not.
criteria.does_not_verify: There are expects, but none of them would fail if the behaviour stated in the title broke.
criteria.cannot_tell_from_file: Whether an expect would fail depends on code, constants or rules that are not visible in this file.
